title: Less packaging, one shop at a time
description: You cannot control how everything is wrapped, but a few steady habits cut the packaging that comes home with you.

body.heading: Start with the bag and the bottle
paragraphs: The two biggest wins are also the oldest advice: a reusable bag you actually remember, and a refillable bottle or coffee cup. Keeping a bag by the door, in the car and in a coat pocket matters more than owning a beautiful one that stays at home.
Habits beat intentions. Attach the reminder to something you never forget, like your keys or your phone, and within a few weeks it stops feeling like an effort.

body.heading: Choose the lighter-wrapped option
paragraphs: Where the same food comes loose or wrapped, loose usually means less packaging and lets you buy exactly the amount you need, which also cuts food waste. Larger packs of dry goods often use less packaging per serving than many small ones, provided you will genuinely use it all.

Refill shops, where you fill your own containers with pasta, grains or cleaning liquids, remove packaging almost entirely. Trying one refill item a month is a gentle way to see whether the routine suits you.

body.heading: Be kind to yourself about the rest
paragraphs: Some packaging protects food, keeps medicine safe or is simply unavoidable where you live. The goal is a downward trend, not purity, and certainly not standing in the aisle feeling guilty.
If a product you love is heavily wrapped, a short polite note to the maker counts for more than silent frustration. Companies track that feedback, and packaging does change when enough customers ask.

takeaway: Remember the bag, choose loose when you can, try one refill, and let the trend matter more than perfection.
